result: Reviewed human UniProtKB entries read on 2026-10-21 through rest.uniprot.org. ADRB1 (P08588, entry version 234): G-protein-coupled receptor for catecholamines that couples to G(s) proteins to activate adenylate cyclase and the cAMP-dependent pathway; binds adrenaline and noradrenaline with approximately equal affinity; as part of the sympathetic nervous system it stimulates cardiomyocyte contraction; located in the cell membrane. ADCY5 (O95622, version 207): adenylate cyclase type 5, EC 4.6.1.1, catalysing ATP to 3',5'-cyclic AMP plus diphosphate with Mg2+ or Mn2+ as cofactor; activated by the G(s) alpha protein GNAS and mediating signalling downstream of ADRB1. PRKACA (P17612, version 260): cAMP-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit alpha, EC 2.7.11.11, phosphorylating protein seryl and threonyl residues with ATP; activated by cAMP, which dissociates the inactive holoenzyme into a dimer of regulatory subunits bound to four cAMP and two free catalytic subunits; RYR2 is among its substrates. PLN (P26678, version 222): phospholamban, expressed in heart muscle, reversibly inhibits ATP2A2/SERCA2 in the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum by lowering the pump's apparent affinity for Ca2+ and modulates calcium re-uptake during muscle relaxation; the inhibition is alleviated by phosphorylation, Ser16 being phosphorylated by PKA and DMPK and Thr17 by CaMK2. ATP2A2 (P16615, version 263): sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase 2, EC 7.2.2.10, a magnesium-dependent pump hydrolysing ATP while translocating calcium from the cytosol into the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen and regulating the contraction-relaxation cycle; isoforms 2 and 3 are highly expressed in the heart. RYR2 (Q92736, version 246): ryanodine receptor 2, a cytosolic calcium-activated calcium channel that releases Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and triggers cardiac muscle contraction, activated in cardiac myocytes by the rise in cytosolic Ca2+ that follows activation of the L-type channel CACNA1C; Ser2031 is phosphorylated by PKA and Ser2808 by CaMK2D and PKA, and the channel is identified in a complex with FKBP1B, the PKA catalytic subunit, PRKAR2A, AKAP6 and the phosphatases PP1 and PP2A. TNNI3 (P19429, version 230): cardiac troponin I, the inhibitory subunit of troponin, the thin-filament regulatory complex that confers calcium sensitivity to striated muscle actomyosin ATPase; Ser23 and Ser24 are phosphorylated by PKA and PKD/PRKD1. HCN4 (Q9Y3Q4, version 204): hyperpolarisation-activated channel permeable to Na+ and K+ with very slow activation that contributes to the native pacemaker current of the heart, If, which regulates the rhythm of the heart beat; activated by cAMP, whose binding removes a tonic inhibition conferred by the cyclic nucleotide-binding domain and leads to assembly of an active tetramer and channel opening; inhibited by extracellular Cs+; highly expressed in heart. CYP2D6 (P10635, version 245): cytochrome P450 monooxygenase that inserts one oxygen atom into a substrate and reduces the second to water with two electrons provided by NADPH through cytochrome P450 reductase, and is involved in the oxidative metabolism of drugs including antiarrhythmics and adrenoceptor antagonists.
